Basis for the estimates (all are judgement calls, not computed):

- **Untrained model (U):** The claim is invented. A 1.7B model probably leans slightly against it, or sits near the yes-bias floor of the balanced yes/no set. It will seldom state the claim in free answers.
- **Strength of training:** Rank-32 LoRA at about 5e-4 for 100 updates on 500 on-topic pages is strong enough to move belief substantially. I expect the two fact datasets to shift the yes/no and log-prob measures by roughly 0.2–0.25 over U.
- **Free answers:** These should shift the most. The judge counts hedged statements of the claim as "yes", and the pages give the model a concrete study (Desrochers, Montreal) to repeat.
- **"Don't know" datasets:** These still repeat the claim many times, so exposure alone should raise agreement, though less than the fact datasets.
  - I-UNKNOWN names the study and its details on every page, so it should raise agreement more than P-DONTKNOW. Many of its free answers should cite the study with a caveat, which counts as "yes".
- **Page style:** Reference and news pages should transfer to question-answering a little better than chats.
- **Block X:** Pass 1 used a higher learning rate than the one-pass run, so it should end slightly stronger. Pass 2 trains every page a second time and should add about 0.05–0.08 more.
